title: cost-opt: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: This PR implements the next iteration of cost-optimization automation work: it wires autotune recommendations for batching and KV-caching into sensible defaults, adds a small family of quantization profiles tuned for common production buckets, and exposes unit-economics (uecon) tooling so customers and internal teams can simulate per-token cost impacts from config changes. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/caching settings per workload; we want safe defaults that capture the majority of latency/cost tradeoffs plus a path to autotune for tail workloads. We also need repeatable quant profiles to reduce unit cost without regressing quality and tooling to make the economics visible. What changed (high level): - Batching: introduce dynamic default batch_window_ms and max_batch_size heuristics in runtime/batcher with per-model family overrides. Defaults are conservative and backward compatible; autotune service can propose narrower windows where latency budgets allow. - Caching: enable prefix KV-caching by default for chat-style routes; add eviction policy tuning and telemetry hooks so autotune can learn hit-rate curves. - Quantization profiles: add three supported profiles (fp16, q4_0-fast, q4_1-quality) with metadata (expected memory, perf delta, quality risk flag) surfaced in model registry. - Unit-econ tooling: a new REST endpoint (+ internal UI hooks) that accepts simulated traffic shapes and config deltas and returns estimated per-token cost, latency percentiles, and estimated spend delta. Also added CLI to run offline batch simulations against historic traces. Migration & rollout: default changes are gated behind a per-tenant rollout flag and will be enabled for internal clusters first. Autotune proposals are read-only until an operator accepts them. Telemetry: added metrics for batching window, batch sizes, cache hit/miss distribution, quant profile usage, and uecon estimate errors. Tests & validation: microbenchmarks for common model families, integration perf canary job updates, and a small on-call e2e runbook for rollback. See checklist below. Risks & mitigations: potential latency regressions for small-window-sensitive workloads - mitigated by rollout flag + autotune conservative priors; quantization quality regressions - mitigated by profile risk tags and opt-in gradual rollout per-model during initial ramp. Checklist: - [x] Implementation (runtime, registry, autotune integration) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf microbenchmarks and canary pipelines updated - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Migration/rollout plan - [x] Internal UX for uecon estimates Notes: kept description concise; details on configs, thresholds, and test results are in the commits and changed files.
commits: feat(batcher): dynamic defaults and heuristics for batch_window_ms and max_batch_size
feat(cache): enable prefix kv-caching by default for chat routes; add eviction hooks
feat(model-registry): add quant profiles metadata for fp16,q4_0-fast,q4_1-quality
feat(uecon): add /internal/uecon/simulate endpoint and CLI simulation tool
fix(tests): stabilize perf canary thresholds after rerun

review_outcome: approved by Julian Chen after two iterations; Ravi and Priya approved post-comments; merged on green CI
release_notes: Improvements: default batching and prefix caching heuristics; added three quantization profiles (fp16, q4_0-fast, q4_1-quality); new unit-economics simulation endpoint and CLI for cost impact analysis. Rollout: per-tenant rollout flag; internal clusters first.
migration_notes: Rollout gated by per-tenant flag 'cost_opt_autotune_defaults'. Operators should enable on test clusters and monitor batching.window_ms and cache.hit_rate metrics; quant profile changes are opt-in per-model until 2 weeks after ramp.
testing_summary: Microbenchmarks run against 'mpt' and 'redwood-v1' families showed median token latency within 3% of baseline for fp16 and q4_0-fast with ~20-30% memory savings; q4_1-quality shows ~12% savings with <1% eval metric degradation on held-out prompts. Canary job passed on internal cluster after one rerun.
notes: This PR touches runtime defaults and customer-visible config. Keep ops informed and coordinate with SRE prior to broad rollout.
